data.name: Pavla
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'pavlos', meaning 'stone' or 'rock'. In Christian tradition, Pavla is the female form of the name Paul, which means 'small' or 'humble' in Latin. This name carries the symbolism of strength, resilience, and steadfastness.
data.spiritual_meaning: Emblem of resilience and steadfastness in the face of challenges.

in_greek.name: Παύλα
in_greek.long_meaning: derived from the Greek root παύο (pauo) meaning 'I have inflicted' or 'I have stopped' and λαός (laos) meaning 'the people'; Paula is a feminine form of the name Paul, which is derived from the same Greek root. The name Pavla may also be considered a diminutive form of Paula, meaning 'little Paul'

in_latin.name: Paula
in_latin.long_meaning: derived from the Latin name Paulus, which is a cognate of the Greek name Paul. Paulus is derived from the Latin word paulus, meaning 'small' or 'humble'

in_english.name: Paula
in_english.long_meaning: derived from the English name Paul, which is derived from the Latin name Paulus. Paulus is a cognate of the Greek name Paul and both names share the same meaning of 'small' or 'humble'

biblical_reference.note: In the New Testament, Pavla is the name of a prominent Christian figure, also known as Paula of Rome or Paula the Deaconess

saint_reference.note: Paula of Rome was a prominent Christian figure and deaconess in the early Christian church. She is traditionally believed to have been the first woman to be buried in an underground tomb within the city of Rome, which was later excavated and revealed to contain a number of inscriptions related to Paula and her association with the apostle Paul
